draft.title: Area of any triangle
card: Area = ½ab sin C. Here a and b are two sides, and C is the angle between them.
It works for any triangle, because a sin C acts as the height. You do not need to measure the height.
Example: sides 8 cm and 5 cm with 30° between them. Area = ½ × 8 × 5 × sin 30° = 20 × 0.5 = 10 cm².
To find an angle from a known area, rearrange to sin C = 2 × Area ÷ ab. Take the inverse sine on your calculator.
draft.remember: Half the product of two sides, times the sine of the angle between them.

a.q: A triangular paddock has two fences of 9 m and 12 m meeting at an angle of 40°. What is its area, to 1 decimal place?
a.why: Area = ½ × 9 × 12 × sin 40° = 54 × 0.6428 = 34.7 m². Using cos 40° gives 41.4 m², which uses the wrong ratio.
a.clue: Half, times both sides, times the sine.

b.q: A triangle has an area of 20 cm². Two of its sides are 8 cm and 10 cm, and the acute angle between them is C. What is C?
b.why: 20 = ½ × 8 × 10 × sin C = 40 sin C, so sin C = 0.5 and C = 30°. Forgetting the ½ gives sin C = 0.25, which is 14.5°.
b.clue: Write the area formula, then solve for sin C.

problems.detail: The card says to find an angle from a known area by taking the inverse sine, but it does not say that 180° minus that angle also fits, because sin C = sin(180° − C). A student could think inverse sine always gives the only answer. Question b avoids this by saying the angle is acute, but the card should note that the obtuse angle may also be a solution.

check.summary: Both questions and their explanations are correct (34.7 m² and 30°). The card should mention that, when finding an angle from an area, the obtuse angle 180° − C can also fit.
